newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Drought fears keep Colombo rubber prices firm.
newsitem.headline: Drought fears keep Colombo rubber prices firm.

text.p: Rubber prices remained strong at this week's Colombo auctions as buyers covered positions in anticipation of lower quantities ahead of the current drought worsens, brokers and exporters said.
The combination of drought and the effects of wintering is likely to keep prices firm, they said.
Wintering is when the tree goes into a period of annual hibernation during the dry months of the first quarter.
"The market is firm. There is very little rubber available," said an exporter. "We could be heading for a drought."

Best latex one-x, the purest grade, increased marginally to 75.60 rupees ($1.32) per kilo on Thursday from 75.20 at the previous auction on Tuesday. Number one fetched 74.75 rupees against 75 rupees on Tuesday. RSS 1 was unquoted on both days.
A total of 198 tonnes of latex crepe and three and a half tonnes of scrap were on offer on Thursday. ($1=57.49 rupees) --Colombo newsroom (941) 434319
